question: Does re-timing on all eight cards at once give the same number as one card at a time?
why_it_is_asked: CLAUDE.md s4 reserves GPU 0 for authoritative timing. What task 01 measured is narrower than 'the node is fine': -0.11% for ONE authoritative timing beside SWEEP work. Eight simultaneous timing runs is a different load, and the node's power envelope pulling clocks down is exactly the mechanism STATE.md D35 is about.
method: Eight problems that already had a GPU-0 number were re-measured with all eight cards running a timing job at once, same iterations (50) and warmup (10), same kernels. Ratio is parallel/solo per workload.
baseline_caveat: The 'solo' numbers were themselves taken on GPU 0 while the fleet sweep occupied cards 1-7. So this compares 'GPU 0 + 7 agent jobs' against '8 concurrent re-times', not against an idle node. T_b, which the score divides by, was measured on an idle node in task 06 -- neither side of this comparison matches that.
verdict: 8-wide is 1.4% SLOWER at the median, and that is systematic rather than noise -- a median sits where it sits. It is 13x task 01's sanctioned sibling interference. In score terms a 1.4% increase in T_k costs about 0.004 of S at S~0.6, against a head-to-head gap between this run and glm-sweep-2 of about 0.03: it does not flip the comparison, and it is about 13% of it.
decision: Used, with the cost recorded on every artifact it produced (`concurrent_cards: 8`) rather than folded in silently. Reversible: deleting the retimed artifacts and re-running serially costs about 1.9 h and nothing else.
